title: Receive a small imposed landing and redirect force forward.
brief: The low drop-to-broad jump is the priority. A grounded snap-down start, a small vertical drop rebound, a received-ball scoop return and supported angled ankle contacts separate eccentric arrival, direction and rapid return. A very small seated single-leg box dose supplies controlled unilateral force without another imposed drop.

explosive.name: Low Drop to Broad Jump
explosive.job: Redirect an externally imposed downward arrival into forward projection.
explosive.cue: Step off a very low stable box, receive on both feet and immediately jump forward; use the needed knee/hip bend, then hold the final landing 2 s.
explosive.regress: Lower the starting step and shorten the forward jump; stop for a stiff/jarring arrival, knee collapse or a deliberate reset between contacts.
explosive.note: Four attempts = four initial drop landings plus four final jump landings; eight events total.

explosive.name: Grounded Snap-Down to Forward Rebound Jump
explosive.job: Create a quick active lowering action and use it for forward force.
explosive.cue: Start tall with arms raised and heels lightly lifted; snap into a shallow athletic position without leaving the floor, then immediately jump forward and hold the final landing.
explosive.regress: Reduce lowering speed/depth and travel; stop if an unintended initial hop appears or the athlete loses the foot base.
explosive.note: No flight in the initial snap-down: only the forward-jump landing counts unless an extra hop actually occurs.

explosive.name: Low Drop to Vertical Rebound
explosive.job: Separate rapid receiving/return from the forward-direction task.
explosive.cue: Step off a very low box, land bilaterally and rebound a modest amount upward; control the final two-foot landing.
explosive.regress: Lower the step and rebound height; stop if impact control or alignment deteriorates.
explosive.note: Two attempts = two initial drop and two final landings; four events total.

explosive.name: Partner-fed Forward Medicine Ball Scoop Return
explosive.job: Use a gentle received load to organize an eccentric-to-forward arm/hip impulse.
explosive.cue: A coach standing offset feeds a very light ball gently to the athlete's low two-hand scoop position; accept it with a small hip/knee bend and promptly throw forward into a clear area, feet planted.
explosive.regress: Use a slower/lighter feed; stop if catching or containment is unreliable or the torso twists.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support
explosive.gate: Competent light-ball receiving and qualified feeder outside the outgoing throw path.
explosive.note: Six catches integrated into six rapid return throws, not an extra catch block.

explosive.name: Wall Ankling Pogo — Bilateral Forward Lean
explosive.job: Practice an angled ankle rebound while hand support limits whole-body drift.
explosive.cue: Hands on a verified fixed wall/support, body in a modest forward lean; make six tiny two-foot ankle rebounds in place with knees soft and trunk aligned.
explosive.regress: Use less lean/amplitude; stop if the support shifts or the athlete collapses through hips/knees.

explosive.name: Seated Single-leg Jump onto a Low Box
explosive.job: Supply a controlled one-leg initial impulse into a two-foot elevated finish.
explosive.cue: Sit still with one foot flat and the other free; push from the supported leg and swing arms to land both feet fully on a very low nearby box; hold and step down.
explosive.regress: Raise the seat or lower/bring the landing box closer while keeping the same task; stop for rocking, twisting or incomplete foot placement.
explosive.gate: Demonstrated single-leg seated takeoff and box landing; no attempt to force height.

control.name: Wall Sit — Shallow Bilateral Hold
control.job: Lightly hold the knee/hip receiving position against a stable support.
control.cue: Back against a fixed wall, feet flat, settle into a comfortable shallow squat and breathe while knees track over feet.
control.regress: Use a higher position; stop for discomfort or a burning/quivering effort.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Tibialis ISO Toe-Up Hold
control.job: Maintain dorsiflexor control for organized foot arrival rather than a loose forefoot slap.
control.cue: Sit with heels planted and lift the forefeet/toes into a comfortable toe-up position; hold gently without curling toes.
control.regress: Lower the lift/effort; stop for cramp or ankle discomfort.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: Drop height is not progressed by calendar or class number. The main task has four attempts and the vertical support only two; both initial drop and final jump landings are counted. A received-ball return and hand-supported ankle work provide different rapid-force tasks instead of six depth-jump variants. The seated unilateral support is only one attempt per side and requires specific competence. Strength returns to modest bilateral anchor doses with reserve; the earlier step-up emphasis is not stacked on this eccentric contact day.
next_job: Class 11 will emphasize fast projection against light external resistance; actual response to the drop contacts must guide readiness and dose.
